issues.summary: Silent money loss on invoice-number casing drift within one invoice. greenBeanInvoices_ builds its groupKey as `supplierKey + '/' + invoiceNum` case-SENSITIVELY (orderapp.gs:436), but the producer only .trim()s invoiceNum (Engine_CostApi.js:527) — it does not lowercase it, unlike supplierKey which costApiSupplierKey_ trims/lowercases/collapses. Meanwhile upsertRows_'s rowKey_ lowercases (Code.gs rowKey_), so the two groups collapse to ONE dedup key and the second is dropped by the `seenInBatch[key] -> duplicatesSkipped++; continue` branch — not summed, not appended, not flagged. Verified empirically by running the two pure functions: two intake lines of the SAME invoice typed 'INV-700' and 'inv-700' produce groups [acme beans/INV-700 = $500, acme beans/inv-700 = $300], both hashing to 'greenbean||acme beans/inv-700'; $500 is ingested and $300 vanishes. Committed spend is silently understated with no flag, no alert and no distinguishing log — duplicatesSkipped is also incremented for routine unchanged rows, so a non-zero value carries no signal. This is the expected input domain, not an exotic one: greenBeanInvoices_ exists precisely because one invoice arrives as several hand-typed lines. Fix: lowercase invoiceNum in the groupKey so the lines merge (and the total is correct), rather than splitting then silently discarding.

The upstream data-quality alert is permanently suppressed once it fires, because its suppression signature counts warnings instead of hashing them: `'warnings:' + upstreamWarnings.length` (orderapp.gs:707). The producer embeds the affected ROW COUNT inside the warning string itself — `droppedNoDate + ' green-bean row(s) were excluded by the date filter'` (Engine_CostApi.js:556) — so the condition escalating from 3 dropped rows to 40 changes the string but leaves the array length at 1, the signature identical, and the alert silent. Round 6's per-page dedup made this strictly worse: before it, a page-count change would at least perturb the length and accidentally re-alert; now the length is pinned. The same blindness hides a wholly DIFFERENT warning replacing an old one at equal count. These are exactly the money-affecting rows the alert exists to surface (dropped rows = understated committed spend). Both sibling alerts already do this correctly — the rename signature hashes full sorted content (orderapp.gs:828) and the flags signature includes flag names (orderapp.gs:733); this one is the odd man out. Hash the sorted warning text, not the count.

Rename detection has an unbounded-snapshot false positive whose runbook destroys real data. The snapshot is built from ALL source='greenbean' rows in the Suppliers tab (orderapp.gs:750-759), which archiveAndPurge_ retains for ARCHIVE_RETENTION_DAYS = 183 (Code.gs:33), while pullSupplierKeys is built only from THIS pull's invoices — a greenBeanWindow_ of roughly 3 months. That leaves a ~3-month band where a supplier's rows are still in Suppliers but the supplier is legitimately absent from the pull (seasonal, or simply no deliveries this quarter). Any invoice-number collision in that band — plausible, since suppliers run independent and often plain-integer numbering sequences — satisfies the heuristic's two conditions (ref is new, prior holder absent from pull) and raises a greenbean_rename alert. The alert asserts the week DOUBLE-COUNTS and instructs 'zero the OLD Suppliers row, then run weeklySummarize' (orderapp.gs:823-828), which applied to a false positive deletes a legitimate historical invoice's spend. Bound the snapshot-side candidates to rows whose storedDate falls inside greenBeanWindow_, so the two sides of the comparison span the same period.

The two new pulls have no liveness monitoring at all — a deleted or never-installed trigger stops both money feeds silently. This diff removes 'shopify' from STALENESS_SOURCES and adds neither 'shopify_orderapp' nor 'greenbean' (staleness.gs:30). orderAppRunSuccess_ still stamps a heartbeat via stalenessStampHeartbeat_ (orderapp.gs:142), so the heartbeat is written but nothing ever reads it. The stated replacement — 'their failure detection is the orderapp fail-open counter/alert' — has a hole: orderAppRunStart_ only increments when a run actually STARTS, so a run that never fires cannot raise the counter, cannot cross ORDERAPP_ALERT_THRESHOLD, and produces no alert. installOrderAppTriggers is a manual editor-run function, making the never-installed case a live possibility during bring-up. The 96h-vs-168h cadence rationale for excluding them is legitimate, but the result is zero coverage, and unlike the analogous 'recurring' gap this one is not recorded in TODO.md (TODO.md:134 covers only recurring). Either add a 168h-aware check or record the gap as a tracked TODO.

The docstring is the more misleading of the two, since it documents the return value of the function directly above it.

The flag-bucketing logic added in 6b4a980 is untested, and its alert text names a flag that cannot occur. orderapp.gs:717-733 builds flagNamesSeen/flagNames and injects them into both the alert body and the suppression signature, but no assertion covers it: test_code.js contains zero occurrences of BLANK_SUPPLIER or INVALID_TIMESTAMP, and the only related assertion (test_code.js:5537-5539) just checks the word UNDERSTATED appears — which passes regardless of whether the distinct flags were bucketed correctly. This is the one piece of business logic in the phase with no test behind it. Separately, the alert body lists INVALID_TIMESTAMP among the flags an operator might see, but the producer drops every null-dateLocal row whenever from/to are supplied (Engine_CostApi.js:545), and this consumer always supplies both — so that flag can never reach flagNames, and those rows surface only through the diagnostics.warnings path instead.

Upstream warnings are discarded on exactly the runs where they would explain the failure. greenBeanFetchAllRows_ accumulates GREENBEAN_UPSTREAM_WARNINGS_ as it pages (orderapp.gs:591-597), but every abort path returns null, and greenBeanPull_impl_ returns { apiFailed: true } at orderapp.gs:693-695 BEFORE the block that reads those warnings and raises the data-quality alert (orderapp.gs:701-710). So a pull that aborts on a size guard, a paging shortfall or a shape failure throws away the upstream diagnostics it already collected — the warnings survive only in the execution log, which is the thing the alert exists to compensate for. Read and surface the warnings before the null-return, or fold them into the failure log line.
